title: Portland teachers to consider unusual 1-year contract deal
author: Julia Silverman
summary: PPS and the Portland Association of Teachers reached a tentative one-year contract for 2026-27, pending ratification by union members and the school board. Teachers would stay on the current salary schedule from July and receive a 2% cost-of-living adjustment starting with the final January paycheck, effectively about 1% for the year, far below the union's latest 7% proposal; other terms of the 2023 post-strike contract would carry over. CFO Michelle Morrison had built the budget assuming a 1% COLA, and the district still faces $56 million in cuts this year and a projected $65 million for 2027-28. The short deal lets the district and union lobby the 2027 Legislature together and aligns PAT's expiration with several other large Oregon districts' unions in June 2027.

title: PPS school board, teachers ratify atypical 1-year contract extension with minimal salary increase
author: Julia Silverman
summary: PAT members and the PPS board both ratified a one-year contract extension for 2026-27, keeping salaries flat until January 2027 and then adding a 2% raise for the last six months, roughly a 1% COLA for the year. The board vote on May 26 was 7-0; PAT reported only that more than half of the 2,090 members voting (about 61% of membership) approved. HR chief Angela Freeman called the deal less than ideal but a building block for the relationship, and PAT president Angela Bonilla credited a more collaborative tone since the superintendency changed. The district still made $56 million in cuts for 2026-27 and projects $65 million for 2027-28, on top of four teacher furlough days this year to close a $14 million midyear gap. Both sides framed the deal as a bridge to a three-year contract after the 2027 legislative session.
